paragraphs:
Mar son of Ravina. Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said, 'A God-fearing person satisfies all the views'—namely Mar son of Ravina, Keitzad Mevarekhin 39b and BaMeh Ishah 61a. Miracles occurred for him: he thirsted, a spring was created, and he drank. Once a violent camel attacked him, and a wall opened up for him, and he went inside, Berakhot 54a. He fasted dream-fasts throughout the year except Purim (Shavuot) and the eve of Yom Kippur—Tosafot and the geonim. Mordekhai writes that he fasted even on festivals, Pesaḥim 68b. He was delicate; his mother made him seven garments for the seven days of the week so a louse would not bite him and interrupt his study, chapter HaDar 65a. At his son's wedding, the sages were excessively merry, and he broke a white glass cup worth four hundred zuz. At his wedding Rav Hamnuna Zuti sang, 'Woe to us, for we shall die': that is, we do not endure as individuals, and must therefore endure as a species, Berakhot 31a. Shoḥer Tov§127 tells this incident of Mar son of Rava.

Throughout the Talmud they took him as an exemplar of piety: 'Is Mar son of Ravina signed upon it?' Yevamot, chapter 2 (22a). In my opinion this was not said because of piety. The passage says Rav Hillel saw Mar bar Ravina's list of secondary forbidden relationships and counted, etc. Rav Ashi told Rav Hillel: who says the statements came from him? He has not signed it, so we cannot know they certainly came from him. He said, 'I raise an objection against Rava's enemies,' Ḥullin 43b. Mar son of Ravina spoke to his son, Ḥelek 106b, Shabbat 80b; and there 145b, Mar son of Ravna. Likewise Berakhot 25b; Shabbat 61a; Kiddushin 39a, 40a; Avodah Zarah 2b; Pesaḥim 33a. See above, Hamnuna Zuta. R. Zeira said, 'I and Mar son of Ravina interpreted,' Nazir 50b. R. Yoḥanan was his brother. Rav Kahana spoke to him. In Rav Naḥman's name, Berakhot 58b. He asked Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak, Shabbat 108a; and Rav Naḥumi bar Zekharyah [the final connection is compressed in the source].
